title: Dynamic hinting prefill scaler and kernel-aware tail mitigations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Improve continuous batching admission and scheduling by using dynamic client-provided hints, runtime length estimators, and kernel-aware scaling rules to reduce tail latency without regressing throughput or cost. This ticket implements a hint-driven prefill scaler that reserves micro-slots for predicted short decodes, routes batches to kernels optimized for trimmed sequence shapes, and adds speculative fallback paths when kernel queues degrade.
background: We see recurrent 95/99th percentile latency spikes on mixed workloads where long-prefill requests monopolize kernel backpressure and cause short requests to wait multiple scheduling cycles. Current admission uses a single global window and conservative shapes; kernel selection is done post-admission which prevents prefill shaping that would match kernel-friendly batch packing. Product and infra teams have reported customer-visible tail regressions on interactive features and higher cost for low-latency tiers.
goals: 1) Reduce P95 by 20% and P99 by 25% for mixed short+long conversational workloads on hosted tier. 2) Maintain or improve token/sec throughput and not increase per-token cost by more than 5%. 3) Provide opt-in SDK hint surface and a safe default when hints are absent.
success_metrics:
- P95 lat drop >= 20% on benchmark flows
- P99 lat drop >= 25% on benchmark flows
- No >5% regression in aggregate token/sec across 24h test run
- Tail incident count reduced by 50% over 2-week canary
non_goals: Does not change underlying kernel implementations or quantization strategies; does not modify billing. This ticket focuses on admission/scaling and routing logic at the runtime orchestration layer.
design_decisions:
- Use client hint preference: expected_tokens (optional) and latency_sensitivity (low/med/high).
- Runtime will run a short (<100ms) local estimator for missing hints using first-token sampling.
- Admission will reserve micro-slots for high-latency_sensitivity short requests (speculative fast-path).
- Kernel selection policy will be consulted during admission to prefer packing shapes that map to fast kernels.
- Add speculative fallback: if chosen kernel queue delay > threshold, immediately re-admit request to a secondary kernel path without prefilling heavy KV cache until decode starts.
implementation_notes:
- New AdmissionController component with hint ingestion, estimator fallback, and reservation allocator.
- AdmissionController exposes metrics: hint_utilization, reservation_fill_rate, speculative_retries.
- Hook kernel profiler endpoint to admission to get live per-kernel queue delay and recent latency histograms.
- Prefill packer to attempt shape-constrained packing (e.g., group short expected_tokens together).
- Add safe default behavior: when hints absent, estimator returns conservative medium-length and no reservation.
- Adjust trace/span instrumentation for prefill decisions to make debugging easier.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated behind runtime flag 'dynamic_prefill_scaler'.
2) Canary to 5% traffic on staging-like clusters for 48h with auto-rollback on metric regressions.
3) Ramp to 25% for 72h with manual pause option.
4) Full roll when P95/P99 steady and no cost regressions.
5) Post-roll monitors and 2-week review.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for reservation allocator and estimator.
- Integration tests simulating mixed short/long request streams with deterministic kernels.
- Load test: 24h replay of real production traces with and without hinting.
- A/B canary comparing P95/P99, token/sec, and cost-per-token.
- Chaos tests: induced kernel slowdowns to verify speculative fallback correctness.
risks:
- Over-reserving micro-slots could reduce throughput if estimator is biased long.
- Speculative re-admission may increase KV cache churn and transient cost.
- Incorrect hint adoption by SDK clients could be gamed, so server must validate hints.
- Instrumentation gaps may make debugging tail causes harder until traces are added.
mitigations:
- Conservative default reservations and decay backoff.
- Rate limit speculative retries per minute per tenant.
- Validate client hints against observed token distribution and clamp outliers.
- Feature flagging and fine-grained observability during canary.
open_questions: What is the right reservation budget per GPU for low-latency slots?
Should we expose a premium latency_sensitivity tier or keep hinting internal only?
How does reservation interact with Dedicated tenant guarantees and preemption?
Can we reuse KV cache across speculative fallback to avoid warmup cost?
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime flag implements admission policy with hint ingestion.
- Benchmarks show required P95/P99 improvements on standard mixed-workload harness.
- No more than 5% token/sec regression in baseline throughput test.
- Canary run with rollbacks exercised and runbook updated.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the estimator correctness and conservative backoff defaults. Pay attention to kernel profiling interface—we need tight, low-noise signals to avoid flip-flopping. Verify the speculative retry safety limits.
